SELECTED_INDEX: 10  
CONFIDENCE: 0.30  
EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows a strong band at 2273 cm⁻¹ together with additional features at 2331 cm⁻¹ and 2415 cm⁻¹, characteristic of C≡N stretching vibrations (often appearing as a Fermi-split doublet/triplet when two or more nitrile groups are present). Among the ten candidates, only molecule 10 (CC(N)C(O)(C#N)C#N) contains any nitrile groups, and it carries two –C≡N substituents, matching the observed multiple bands in the 2250–2450 cm⁻¹ region.  

Further support:  
• Broad/medium bands at 3225 and 3258 cm⁻¹ match N–H/O–H stretches expected for the amino and hydroxyl functions present in 10.  
• Strong C–H stretches at 2928 and 2985 cm⁻¹ are consistent with the aliphatic methyl groups of 10.  
• Bands near 1458 cm⁻¹ (CH₃ deformation) and 1588 cm⁻¹ (NH₂ scissoring / H-bonded OH bend) fit the functional groups in 10.  

No other candidate possesses nitrile groups, making compound 10 the only structure compatible with the key 2273–2415 cm⁻¹ region.
